Subject: GPU commitment playbook for priority deals

Team —

Following up from yesterday's planning touchpoint. I put together a short playbook (attached) that maps how we want to translate near-term pipeline commitments into Dedicated GPU reservations for Q4. High-level ask: please review the workbook and confirm the knobs below by EOD Friday so we can lock a preliminary capacity request to infra.

Scope / decisions we need this week:
- Commitment bands: 0-50k / 50-200k / 200k+ monthly token units and what GPU pool to map them to (reserved / burst).
- Buffer policy: per-deal % buffer (suggest 20% for enterprise pilots, 10% for pilots in self-serve).
- Conversion assumptions: tokens -> GPU hours per model family (sheet tab 2).
- Approval path: finance sign-off cadence and any manual review thresholds.

I've attached: gpu_commitment_playbook.xlsx (summary + per-deal tabs). I also exported the current HubSpot deal list (attached) so numbers line up with CRM.

Quick notes on two priority deals that should influence the bands:
- Acme Corp (RD-2028-ACME-01): pilot + PoC starting Sept; they want reserved capacity for latency SLAs.
- Globex (RD-2028-GLOBEX-07): large POC but flexible on burst; procurement looped in.

Please add comments in the sheet and reply with any redlines to assumptions. If infra has hard constraints that change the bands, call that out.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Head, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: gpu_commitment_playbook.xlsx

Subject: Re: GPU commitment playbook for priority deals

Monica / Ben —

Thanks for the playbook. A few infra constraints and proposals so finance/sales know the knobs: 
- We have two meaningful pools for this ask: low-latency pinned (reserved nodes with static allocation) and elastic burst (shared pools with autoscale). Pinned nodes have ~10% higher cost but guaranteed tail latency.
- Minimum reservation unit is a 4-GPU block on our Dedicated offering due to current placement bin-packing (we can simulate splitting but it increases fragmentation). That suggests we should prefer mapping deals to bands that align to multiples of 4 GPUs.
- Buffer recommendation: 15% system-level buffer beyond deal-level buffers to handle multi-tenant transient spikes.
- Ramp cadence: infra can commit to a weekly ramp plan with checkpoints (Week 0/2/4) if sales provides a pinned ramp schedule.

Operational overhead: smaller, many micro-commitments increase allocation churn and manual reconciliation with finance. If we accept 4-GPU minimum chunks, that reduces churn but requires smoothing deals into committed windows.

I'll attach a short diagram (infra_capacity_map.pdf) showing pool characteristics. Happy to walk through on Friday.

-Karthik
Head of Fleet Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: infra_capacity_map.pdf

Subject: Re: GPU commitment playbook for priority deals

Monica —

I reviewed the workbook and infra notes. Finance perspective: we need to formalize the approval gates and cost model before any reservation is signed. A couple of points: 
- Cost bands: map the three commitment bands to three billing tiers with clear overage pricing. We can't sign reserved contracts without a single-line expected monthly spend per deal.
- Approvals: any deal > $75k/month needs VP sign-off; between $25k-$75k monthly needs finance manager approval; below $25k can be approved by Sales Ops.
- Accounting: reservations will be capitalized differently depending on the term; procurement/legal will need a heads-up for multi-quarter commitments.

I'll add comments directly in the sheet (link below). Please feed the per-deal expected monthly spend into tab 'Finance Input'. If sales can lock those numbers by EOD Monday we can present to VP Ops on Tuesday.

GSheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1A2bGpuCommitmentPlaybook

Laura Bennett

Thanks all — quick consolidation and next steps: 

Decisions captured so far (working draft):
- Bands: 0-50k (tier A), 50-200k (tier B), 200k+ (tier C).
- Mapping: Tier C -> pinned low-latency pool (min 4-GPU blocks). Tier B -> recommend 4-GPU reserved blocks or burst mix. Tier A -> burst pool unless customer requires pinned.
- Buffers: deal-level buffer 10% pilot / 20% enterprise; system-level buffer 15%.
- Finance gates: Laura's approval thresholds accepted.

Action items:
1) Ben: populate Finance Input tab with expected monthly spend for Acme + Globex by EOD Monday.
2) Karthik: confirm which physical pools can host pinned low-latency instances and if we can offer a 2-GPU reserved option as a special case (answer needed by Monday).
3) Laura: prepare VP sign-off slide deck (I can help with a short one-pager).
4) Priyom: I'll need a consolidated email to procurement/legal for the two priority deals once spend is confirmed.

I'll update the sheet with the working draft and lock comments. Jessica (Acme) — including you here so you see the proposed mapping; we'll confirm your ramp schedule next week.

Monica Patel
Head, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
